newsitem.title: GREECE: GREECE TO ISSUE 5, 10-YR CPI-LINKED BONDS AUG 11.
newsitem.headline: GREECE TO ISSUE 5, 10-YR CPI-LINKED BONDS AUG 11.

text.p: Greece will issue five- and 10-year inflation-linked bonds paying a fixed 4.0 percent above the consimer price index (CPI) through a public offering on August 11, the finance ministry said in a statement.
"State index-linked bonds will be offered to the investment public for the second time through a public subscription," it said. "The securities will be in dematerialised form."
Dematerialised form means the bonds will not trade in a physical form. Instead, they will be book entries.

Greece first issued inflation-protected bonds on May 20, 1997 raising 70 billion drachmas ($239.7 million). The bonds had maturities of five and 10 years with a coupon of 4.0 percent, taxed at 7.5 percent.
The finance ministry's target for 1997 is to raise 300 billion drachmas.
The reference CPI for the bonds will be the official CPI released by the National Statistics Service (NSS) early each month.
The coupons are annual. --George Georgiopoulos, Angelos Kiosklis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
